Detailed method

The calculator opens at 500 g flour, 62% hydration, 2.2% salt, and 0.4% yeast. That is 310 g water, 11 g salt, and 2 g yeast, 823 g of dough. The balls fields open at 4 pieces of 206 g. Divide it into 4 folded pies. The filling is extra and is not in the gram total. At 62% the dough is a little stiffer than an open round, so the seam can close. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 310 g water, 11 g salt, and 2 g instant yeast, then knead for about 8 minutes until smooth. At 62% the dough is soft and holds a firm ball. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Rise Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 80 to 110 minutes. With 0.4% yeast it should grow by about half to nearly double. One fold halfway through is enough.
  3. Divide Cut 4 pieces of 206 g, the weight in the balls fields. Cover them and rest 15 minutes.
  4. Fill Dust the counter lightly and press each piece into a round about 20 cm across. On one half, add about 80 g of filling, such as cheese and a cooked topping. Leave a bare border. The filling is extra and is not in the gram total. Too much filling tears the seam.
  5. Seal Brush the border with water, fold the empty half over, and press the edge shut. Crimp it so it stays closed. Cut one small slit in the top.
  6. Bake Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F). Bake 16 to 20 minutes, until the crust is deep golden and the sealed edge is firm.
  7. Rest Wait about 5 minutes before you cut. The filling is hotter than the crust.
